episodes.title: AI researchers debate what we should do next – Daniel Kokotajlo and Ege Erdil
episodes.description: New podcast episode between Ege Erdil and Daniel Kokotajlo. I thought this was going to be a debate, but they ended up agreeing on a lot more than I expected. Their main point of disagreement is how likely it is that we get some intelligence explosion that gives us AIs more competent than any human expert before 2029. Ege puts this possibility at around 20%, whereas Daniel thinks it’s higher than 50%. They agree that there is not a huge difference in probability, and that, in either case, the situation is crazy enough that our civilization really needs to grapple with how the world might be transformed, and we need a plan that actually makes sense. episodes.title: Replay: From Swipe to Scale: How Tinder Became #1 (2024)
episodes.description: How do you build a network product when it only works if everyone around you is already using it? Originally recorded in 2024, Tinder founder Sean Rad explains how the company went from a few hundred users to the world’s #1 dating app. Sean joins a16z General Partner Andrew Chen to unpack Tinder’s early product decisions, why the team avoided mass marketing in favor of building density on college campuses, and how the swipe experience grew out of designing specifically for mobile. They also discuss why product-market fit has to come before marketing, how Tinder learned from failed features, and why listening to users mattered more than competitors or the press. episodes.title: Isabella Weber's Vision for an Affordability Agenda
episodes.description: The most important word in politics right now is affordability. It was a winning issue in the midterms for Democrats, and one of the reasons why people across Europe are out in the streets protesting: Food, housing, and energy are getting more expensive by the day. During the height of the pandemic, we talked a lot about inflation with Isabella Weber, and her on what governments can do to make life more affordable has evolved into a book called Anti-Fascist Economics: In Defense of Affordability, Dignity, and Democracy. It is part-history, part-manifesto, and it maps out why things got so expensive and what can be done to get prices down. episodes.title: 【Y Combinator採択】商社を辞めて漁師、アメリカで水産×AI起業／Asakana 共同創業者 松岡 裕大さん
episodes.description: 三菱商事でマグロやカツオを扱い、退職後は鹿児島のブリの養殖場で漁師に。マッキンゼーを経てアメリカで起業し、4回目の応募でY Combinatorに採択されました。日本人の起業家が集まって暮らすサンフランシスコのテックハウスで、話を伺いました。 今回のゲストは、Asakana 共同創業者の松岡 裕大さん。Asakanaは、北米の食品卸売業者に向けて、レストランからメール・テキスト・電話・ボイスメールで届く注文をAIが読み取り、基幹システムに入力するサービスを提供しています。2026年秋のY Combinator（Fall 2026）に採択されました。 魚との原点は5歳のころ。祖父との釣りで、取りすぎたイワシを海に捨てて叱られた経験です。大学時代のアメリカ留学では、日本の魚のおいしさは締め方とコールドチェーンにあると気づきます。三菱商事に入り、「魚をやらせてくれ」と頼んで水産部へ。退職後は朝4時から働く漁師の3ヶ月を過ごし、マッキンゼー、コロンビア大学ビジネススクールのMBAへと進みました。 鮮度を測る機械から、現場のやり方を変えずに注文入力を自動化する今の事業にたどり着くまで。Googleに8年在籍し、Geminiの開発にも携わったBenjamin Solis-Cohenさんと、YCの共同創業者マッチングで出会った経緯。4回目の挑戦でYCに採択された決め手と、採択後の毎日。 「辛くなければ人生ではない」という考え方、食品業界の利益率を上げたいという思い、そして日本の視聴者への「もっとリスクを取ってほしい」というメッセージまで。商社から漁師、コンサル、MBAを経てYCにたどり着いた道のりと、食品業界で実現したい未来を伺いました。 ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ ▼ タイムスタンプ 00:00 ダイジェスト 00:44 オープニング：サンフランシスコのテックハウスから
